mn37:5.5: whether that spirit comprehended what the Buddha said when he agreed with him, or not?”
mn37:10.2: In the same way, when Sakka’s maids saw Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, being discreet and prudent, each went to her own bedroom.
mn37:15.4: ‘Sir, how do you briefly define a mendicant who is freed through the ending of craving, who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal, and is best among gods and humans?’
mn37:15.5: When he had spoken, Moggallāna, I said to Sakka, lord of gods,
mn37:15.6: ‘Lord of gods, it’s when a mendicant has heard:
mn37:15.8: Lord of gods, when a mendicant has heard that
mn37:15.10: they directly know all things. Directly knowing all things, they completely understand all things. Having completely understood all things, when they experience any kind of feeling—pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral—
mn37:15.11: they meditate observing impermanence, dispassion, cessation, and letting go in those feelings.
mn37:15.12: Meditating in this way, observing impermanence, dispassion, and cessation in those feelings,
mn37:15.13: and observing letting go, they don’t grasp at anything in the world.
mn37:15.14: Not grasping, they’re not anxious. Not being anxious, they personally become extinguished.
mn37:15.15: They understand: “Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.”
mn37:15.16: That’s how I briefly define a mendicant who is freed through the ending of craving, who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal, and is best among gods and humans.’
mn37:15.20: The Shorter Discourse on the Ending of Craving is finished—the seventh.
